rows.title: As the school year begins online, thousands of Texas students are being left out of virtual learning
rows.standfirst: One Central Texas superintendent estimated that up to 7,000 students in his district struggled to access virtual learning, and new iPads are not likely to arrive before October. In South Texas, students share computers, phones and spotty internet with siblings.

rows.title: “In survival mode”: How some evacuees are still dealing with the dual challenge of a hurricane and a recession
rows.standfirst: Many Southeast Texans were already struggling through a pandemic and its parallel recession. Then came Hurricane Laura and officials’ evacuation orders.

rows.title: Texas mayors warn pandemic’s effects on city budgets will linger for years
rows.standfirst: The temporary closure of businesses and high levels of unemployment due to the pandemic have caused sales tax revenues — which make up a significant portion of cities’ budgets — to plummet.

rows.title: Texas coronavirus hospitalizations are at a two-month low, but school reopenings pose new risks
rows.standfirst: After a late July peak, the number of statewide coronavirus hospitalizations has fallen from about 11,000 per day to about 4,500. Children who are infected are less likely to be hospitalized.

rows.title: With time running out, Texas abruptly launches a $15 million ad campaign chasing an accurate census count
rows.standfirst: After rejecting efforts to spend state money on outreach to help ensure an accurate census count, Republican leaders are now dipping into federal coronavirus relief funds to pay for a last-minute ad campaign.

rows.title: Texans spent less going out to eat and drink, but more on home improvement as coronavirus cases peaked this summer
rows.standfirst: The state collected 5.6% less in sales tax revenue last month than in August 2019. The expiration of some federal relief aid could mean more decreases in coming months.

rows.title: Pandemic politics ripple through Texas races, forcing U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw to defend his coronavirus response
rows.standfirst: In Crenshaw’s bid for reelection, the fight over masks and rhetoric has become particularly pitched, drawing in dozens of Houston-area doctors.

rows.title: Susan Rice condemns recent violence at protests, says she does not support defunding police
rows.standfirst: Speaking at The Texas Tribune Festival, Rice said she supported “reimagining the role of police” and reallocating funds to social and economic development in some cities.

rows.title: Millions of Texans could be shielded from evictions under new Trump administration order
rows.standfirst: A previous federal order, which only protected renters in federally backed housing, expired in July.

rows.title: Analysis: With schools opening, Texas enters a critical two weeks of the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Texas is poised right now as it was in late April: COVID-19 numbers are moving in the right direction, and reopenings — schools this time — are underway. Everyone’s hoping for a different result this time.

rows.title: Privately built border wall will fail, engineering report says
rows.standfirst: The report, set to be filed in federal court this week, confirms reporting from ProPublica and The Texas Tribune that found portions of the wall were in danger of overturning if not fixed due to extensive erosion just months after it was built.

rows.title: Absent widespread testing, Texas schools have limited tools to prevent coronavirus spread
rows.standfirst: Coronavirus cases are inevitable as Texas schools reopen. The challenge for administrators will be preventing large-scale outbreaks.

rows.title: Texas A&M President Michael Young says he will retire May 31 to return to faculty
rows.standfirst: Young will continue as a faculty member for the Bush School of Government and Public Service and the Texas A&M School of Law, and take on a new role as the director of the Institute for Religious Liberties and International Affairs.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court temporarily blocks Harris County from sending mail-in ballot applications to all its voters
rows.standfirst: The Harris County Republican Party had sued to stop the county from sending the absentee ballot applications.

rows.title: Report: Harris County’s bail reforms let more people out of jail before trial without raising risk of reoffending
rows.standfirst: Texas’ most populous county changed its bail practices for misdemeanor defendants last year after a lengthy lawsuit challenging cash bail.

rows.title: Analysis: Voting in Texas could be as easy as a trip to the grocery store
rows.standfirst: Some of the biggest private-sector companies in Texas adapted quickly to customer service during the pandemic. Unfortunately, they’re not in charge of voting.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott considering legislation to put Austin police under state control after budget cut
rows.standfirst: If passed, the legislative proposal could consolidate Austin’s police department under the Texas Department of Public Safety.

rows.title: After a teen’s death, Texas cuts ties with a rural foster care facility, then gets a tongue-lashing from a federal judge
rows.standfirst: In the first day of a two-day hearing to evaluate progress the state has made toward resolving a long-running foster care lawsuit, U.S. District Judge Janis Jack excoriated Texas child welfare officials.

rows.title: In Texas, President Trump’s team hits the road to shore up support
rows.standfirst: The president’s reelection campaign launched a bus tour of the state Thursday, though surrogates said — strenuously — that they still don’t see Texas in play.

rows.title: Assistant Texas attorney general loses job after report surfaces racist tweets
rows.standfirst: Nick Moutos threatened Black Lives Matter protesters and has regularly referred to the organizers as “terrorists.” He called Islam a “virus” and trans people an “abomination.”

rows.title: Dallas and Harris county judges criticize Gov. Greg Abbott’s coronavirus response for putting politics ahead of science
rows.standfirst: At The Texas Tribune Festival, Clay Jenkins and Lina Hidalgo, both Democrats, said local officials and health experts stepped into a leadership vacuum left by state and federal leaders.

rows.title: No, a Texas man was not indicted for filling out 1,700 mail-in ballots, despite what Attorney General William Barr said
rows.standfirst: The case at issue stems from a 2017 investigation into suspected mail-in voter fraud in Dallas County.

rows.title: Texas should update sex education standards
rows.standfirst: As physicians, social workers, youth-serving professionals, and teen pregnancy prevention advocates, we urge the State Board of Education to adopt health education standards on reproductive health next week.

rows.title: Federal judge says she will again hold Texas in contempt of court for failing to meet foster care reforms
rows.standfirst: Federal Judge Janis Jack hammered state child welfare officials during a two-day hearing over what she called failures to improve Texas’ foster care system.

rows.title: Celebrating Our #TribFest20 Anniversary … with Data
rows.standfirst: Without data, you’re just a person with an opinion. So, Texas 2036 partnered with The Texas Tribune on our FAST FACTS video series, illuminating big issues facing Texas.

rows.title: ACLU warns 500 Texas school districts to revise discriminatory dress codes
rows.standfirst: The letter comes two weeks after a federal judge blocked the Barbers Hill Independent School District from keeping a dress code policy that advocates have called racist.

rows.title: A week after hurricane evacuation, nursing home residents with COVID-19 are still waiting to return to East Texas
rows.standfirst: More than 500 residents of nursing homes, assisted living facilities and other long-term care centers who were evacuated are still waiting to come home, according to the state.

rows.title: In Texas, Republicans fight voting by mail expansion while encouraging their voters to use it
rows.standfirst: What was once a lightly used and largely uncontroversial voting option in Texas, one even Republicans relied on, is now the crux of the latest fight over who gets to vote and, equally as crucial in a pandemic, who has access to safe voting.

rows.title: An Austin doctor got a COVID-19 test from his own company. They billed his insurance company nearly $11,000
rows.standfirst: Physicians Premier ER charged Dr. Zachary Sussman’s insurance $10,984 for his COVID-19 antibody test even though Sussman worked for the chain and knows the testing materials only cost about $8. Even more surprising: The insurer paid in full.

rows.title: “It’s pretty hard to learn how to draw an IV online”: This nursing student is grateful for hands-on training this semester
rows.standfirst: In the weekend edition of The Brief podcast, listen to why a University of Texas at Austin sophomore says attending in-person labs during the pandemic is worth the risk.

rows.title: Coronavirus cases postpone TCU-SMU game, the season’s first college football matchup involving a Texas Big 12 team
rows.standfirst: The game had been scheduled for Sept. 11.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court rejects Republicans’ attempt to remove 44 Libertarians from the November ballot
rows.standfirst: The GOP sued because the Libertarians didn’t pay their filing fees. But the state Supreme Court said Republicans missed the deadline to kick them off the ballot.

rows.title: Judge temporarily halts efforts to end census count early
rows.standfirst: The ruling is the first in a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s plans to wind down the count a month early. Democrat-led Harris County joined the challenge last month.

rows.title: Student athletes get COVID-19 tests three times a week, while experts say testing for other university students is lagging
rows.standfirst: Public health experts say colleges need to dramatically ramp up testing in order to catch “silent spread” fueled by students who are infected but don’t have symptoms.

rows.title: Texas universities blame off-campus parties for rising COVID-19 cases, but few are disciplining students
rows.standfirst: Schools, desperate to keep their doors open but worried about health risks to their students, are being put in the uncomfortable position of having to govern young adult behavior that is mostly happening off university property.

rows.title: Many Texas students will return to classrooms Tuesday. Little will be normal.
rows.standfirst: As students across Texas return to schools for in-person classes, there will be masks, distancing and lunches eaten at desks. Many students will remain at home, joining in on laptops and phones.

rows.title: National Democratic group to spend $6.2 million in effort to flip the Texas House
rows.standfirst: The super PAC, Forward Majority, is pouring the money into 18 races that will likely determine which party controls the lower chamber in January.

rows.title: Texas is revising its sex education standards, but they’ll likely remain silent on LGBTQ issues
rows.standfirst: The Republican-dominated State Board of Education is taking up the first revision of sex ed curriculum in more than 20 years. LGBTQ students say they’re being excluded again.

rows.title: Watch Houston Police Chief Art Acevedo talk about race, police reform at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: Acevedo also discussed the reverberations of George Floyd’s death in the city where Floyd was raised.

rows.title: Congressional subcommittees will investigate Fort Hood’s leadership after a string of deaths
rows.standfirst: “Where appropriate, we intend to seek justice on behalf of those in uniform,” the subcommittee chairs said while announcing their probe of the Texas Army base.

rows.title: Dallas Police Chief Reneé Hall resigns following criticisms of protest response
rows.standfirst: Hall implied that “inquiries about future career opportunities” were a reason for leaving the Dallas Police Department. In 2017, she became the first woman to head the force.

rows.title: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit that sought sweeping changes to Texas’ in-person voting rules
rows.standfirst: Two civil rights groups and two Texas voters had asked a federal judge to require substantial changes to polling place procedures, including an across-the-board mask mandate and expanded curbside voting.

rows.title: Texas ordered to immediately fix flaws in method used to reject some mail-in ballots
rows.standfirst: When local election officials throw out a mail-in ballot because they think a signature is suspect, the voter must have a meaningful chance to contest the decision, a federal judge ruled.

rows.title: Analysis: In close elections, two opponents can be better than one
rows.standfirst: A Republican effort to knock 44 Libertarians off the ballot fell short, and that could have an outsize effect on close races in November.

rows.title: Texans with developmental disabilities in state homes still don’t have visitors. Their parents worry they don’t know why.
rows.standfirst: Across Texas, families with loved ones in state supported living centers are desperate for in-person visits after months have ticked by with coronavirus restrictions in place.

rows.title: With colorful masks and many new rules, Mrs. Hogan’s “honeybees” arrive for kindergarten
rows.standfirst: In-person classes resumed at Highland Village Elementary School on Tuesday. The youngest students wore masks printed with pepperoni pizza and Polly Pocket, adjusting to new safety protocols.

rows.title: Texas physicians are losing money during the pandemic. They want lawmakers to make health insurers pay up.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Academy of Family Physicians is also asking legislators to expand Medicaid insurance coverage to low-income adults and restore funding for a program that studied racial health disparities.

rows.title: It’s time to save Texas wineries and distilleries
rows.standfirst: The Texas Winery PAC and the Texas Craft Spirits PAC urge Texas to support laws that promote rather than inhibit the growth of the craft spirits and wine industries.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott calls on all Texas candidates to sign pledge against police budget cuts
rows.standfirst: The pledge is the governor’s latest political move in an election season consumed by debates on policing reforms and funding.

rows.title: The Ruger 10/22
rows.standfirst: By Guns.com In today’s unboxing video, we take a look at a classic, the Ruger 10/22. The Ruger 10/22 comes in many forms and variations and we’re showing off just a few of the models from the Guns.com vault. Ruger 10/22 unboxing

rows.title: Donald Trump says Ted Cruz is on his list of potential second-term Supreme Court picks
rows.standfirst: James Ho, a Texan who serves on the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, is also on the list of 20 potential justices.

rows.title: Unemployed Texans will no longer receive an extra $300 in weekly payments
rows.standfirst: The Federal Emergency Management Agency notified state officials Wednesday that the payments for out-of-work Texans have ended, according to the Texas Workforce Commission, which handles unemployment claims.

rows.title: As Congress weighs a new coronavirus aid bill, will U.S. citizens from mixed-status families get left out again?
rows.standfirst: U.S. citizens who have undocumented family members were barred from receiving stimulus checks earlier this year. They’re hoping that Congress doesn’t leave them out again.

rows.title: “My story does resonate”: Candace Valenzuela wants to flip a Republican seat and become the first Black Latina in Congress
rows.standfirst: Valenzuela is running for a North Texas seat long held by Republicans. But the shifting political winds in the suburbs are giving Democrats hope.

rows.title: Watch live: Gov. Greg Abbott signs pledge against cutting police budgets in Texas at 2 p.m.
rows.standfirst: Abbott has called on all Texas candidates in the November election to sign it to show they are “backing the blue.” Other state leaders will join him Thursday at the Austin Police Association.

rows.title: UT-Austin says it will require only student ticket holders to test negative for COVID-19 before Saturday’s football game
rows.standfirst: Other ticket holders and visitors from University of Texas at El Paso are not required to be tested to enter the stadium.

rows.title: As energy secretary, Rick Perry mixed money and politics in Ukraine. The deals could be worth billions.
rows.standfirst: When the then-energy secretary accidentally helped lead the president into impeachment, he was simultaneously trying to help his friends cash in on a big gas deal.

rows.title: U.S. Sen. John Cornyn suggests Trump could’ve struck a better balance in discussing early coronavirus threat
rows.standfirst: Cornyn’s comments Thursday came in response to the recent revelation that the president intentionally downplayed the severity of the pandemic.

rows.title: How Gov. Greg Abbott made Austin’s police budget cuts a top campaign issue for candidates running in November
rows.standfirst: The Republican governor isn’t on the November ballot. But he has come out hard against efforts to shift city money away from policing, echoing a national debate on policing and crime during a tumultuous election season.

rows.title: Federal court blocks Trump effort to exclude undocumented immigrants when congressional seats are divvied up
rows.standfirst: Trump’s bid to exclude undocumented immigrants from population counts for redistricting could cost Texas three seats in Congress. Thursday’s ruling could still be appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court.

rows.title: Federal appeals court rejects Texas Democrats’ effort to expand voting by mail
rows.standfirst: The Texas Democratic Party had challenged the state’s age limits on voting by mail, arguing that they violated the 26th Amendment’s protections against voting restrictions that discriminate based on age.

rows.title: Analysis: College football is back — as both a spectacular and a science experiment
rows.standfirst: College football is starting back up with a new burden: It’s the most visible evidence of the wisdom of putting Texas students back on campus.

rows.title: The percentage of Texans testing positive for COVID-19 is dropping, but experts say the threat isn’t over
rows.standfirst: One key COVID-19 metric is trending downward, but experts worry that Labor Day gatherings and school reopenings could cause cases to spike again.

rows.title: Texas schools seeing steep declines in number of students getting free meals
rows.standfirst: Many families with students learning at home can’t access the free breakfasts and lunches they depended on when their children were attending school in person.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Brian Babin defends Trump’s early coronavirus statements, comparing them to FDR’s after Pearl Harbor
rows.standfirst: During The Texas Tribune Festival, Babin and U.S. Rep. Michael Burgess both backed the president after revelations from a forthcoming book by journalist Bob Woodward.

rows.title: Texas judge allows Harris County to send all voters applications for mail-in ballots
rows.standfirst: State district judge R.K. Sandill rejected the state’s request for a temporary injunction to bar Harris County from pursuing its mailing plan.

rows.title: Lawmakers call on Gov. Greg Abbott to plan to expand broadband access as pandemic worsens disparities
rows.standfirst: A bipartisan group of 88 state lawmakers said in a letter that a statewide broadband plan is well overdue.

rows.title: Texas education board rejects three new charter school operators, greenlights five others
rows.standfirst: Opponents told the board that allowing more charter operators will drain money from traditional public schools, but some parents believe charters offer their children better educations.

rows.title: Texas gives preliminary approval for revised school sex ed policy that excludes LGBTQ issues
rows.standfirst: After marathon meetings over three days, the Republican-dominated board also rejected efforts to teach students about consent. It is expected to take a final vote in November.

rows.title: Texas Democrats from the border team up for new PAC in effort to flip the state House
rows.standfirst: The group, Corazón de la Frontera PAC, is being organized by El Paso Rep. Joe Moody, the House speaker pro tem.

rows.title: Texas college football returns with thousands of fans in the stadiums as campus cases grow
rows.standfirst: The University of Texas at Austin will face off against The University of Texas at El Paso on Saturday with thousands of fans in the stadium and new safety precautions.

rows.title: Texas eased restrictions for nursing homes — but she still can’t see her mom and knows that isolation can be deadly
rows.standfirst: Jimmie Arnold’s mother-in-law and mother were in the same nursing home in Bryan when Gov. Greg Abbott barred all visitation to limit the spread of the coronavirus. In the weekend edition of The Brief podcast, listen to why Arnold says after six months, it’s taking its toll.

rows.title: “It’s like walking into a ghost town”: Under tight pandemic restrictions, college football returns to Austin
rows.standfirst: With just over 15,000 fans in a stadium that holds more than 100,000, the University of Texas kicked off the football season after requiring mandatory COVID-19 tests for students who attended the game.

rows.title: Analysis: Elections are fights, settled by voters. This one is no exception.
rows.standfirst: Elections are about differences, about making friends look good and foes look bad. And that’s why you’re not hearing a lot of talk right now about solutions. The candidates are talking about problems instead.

rows.title: Biden campaign adds more staff in Texas
rows.standfirst: The campaign has added 13 more members to its team in Texas, where polls continue to point to a close race against President Donald Trump.

rows.title: Watch Nikole Hannah-Jones and Wesley Lowery on the 1619 Project and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: Hannah-Jones, a staff writer at The New York Times Magazine, and Lowery, a correspondent for 60 Minutes’ “60 in 6,” also discussed racial disparities during the pandemic and the fight for a true democracy.

rows.title: Ted Cruz says he doesn’t want to join the Supreme Court after being shortlisted by Trump
rows.standfirst: Last week, President Donald Trump named Cruz and another Texan to a list of potential picks for the U.S. Supreme Court if he gets a second term.

rows.title: Thousands of immigrants in Texas could be forced to leave the country following court decision on protected status
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration wants to end Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of thousands of people from a number of countries who received protection because of armed conflicts and natural disasters.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Ron Wright, of Arlington, hospitalized due to complications from cancer treatment
rows.standfirst: The freshman member of Congress has been undergoing treatment for lung cancer since last year.

rows.title: Texas officials change how the state reports positivity rate after testing backlogs skewed coronavirus data
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of State Health Services said it will now rely on a calculation that takes into account the date on which a coronavirus test was administered, rather than when it was reported.

rows.title: Here’s your Texas 2020 November ballot
rows.standfirst: The 2020 U.S. election will take place Nov. 3. See the full list of candidates in Texas, and find out who’s on your ballot based on where you live.

rows.title: Watch U.S. Sen. Marco Rubio discuss the 2020 election and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: Rubio, R-Florida, the acting chair of the U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee, alsoed discuss immigration and national security.

rows.title: Texas officials walk back $15 million proposed cuts to women’s and children’s health services
rows.standfirst: The changes to the budget proposal come after lawmakers and advocates protested the previous plan would hurt vulnerable Texans.

rows.title: John Cornyn, MJ Hegar set for first debate, though Hegar wants two more
rows.standfirst: Cornyn previously said he’s open to debating Hegar more than once, and his campaign said Tuesday it looks “forward to considering other opportunities.”

rows.title: Penhole: Democracy Made Easy
rows.standfirst: Pin down the true political picture with a few taps. For those seeking more straightforward political facts, a new app from a Dallas startup has you covered.

rows.title: ICE deported a key witness in investigation of sexual assault and harassment at El Paso detention center
rows.standfirst: Department of Homeland Security and Justice Department inspectors general are investigating allegations that ICE guards assaulted detainees in camera blind spots.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court rules 3 Green Party candidates should be added back to November ballot
rows.standfirst: Democrats successfully sued last month to remove from the ballot the Green Party nominees for U.S. Senate, Railroad Commission and the 21st Congressional District.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court again blocks Harris County from sending mail-in ballot applications to all voters
rows.standfirst: The Supreme Court granted the Texas attorney general’s request to temporarily halt the county’s mailing of applications while the case is appealed. A separate order blocking the effort was set to end this week.

rows.title: Analysis: It’s hard to make good pandemic policy if the Texas data is fuzzy
rows.standfirst: The state’s public health experts are changing their calculation of one of the governor’s go-to measures of the spread of coronavirus. It’s an improvement, but the new version has some bugs of its own.

rows.title: Balancing higher health risks and spotty internet, reopening college in the Rio Grande Valley is a challenge
rows.standfirst: At UT-Rio Grande Valley, administrators spent a tense summer preparing for the fall semester while local coronavirus rates spiked, the area spiraled into further economic depression and debate raged across the nation about how to safely send college students back to school.

rows.title: The law in a time of uncertainty
rows.standfirst: The Barrister is an occasional newsletter by the attorneys at Amini & Conant, providing practical legal news and advice, right to your inbox.

rows.title: Watch John Cornyn and MJ Hegar debate the pandemic, police reform and voting
rows.standfirst: U.S. Sen. John Cornyn, a three-term Republican incumbent, and Democratic challenger MJ Hegar, answered the same set of questions for our “Split Decision” virtual debate series.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott used pandemic as cover to ban abortions in Texas, former Planned Parenthood head says
rows.standfirst: Cecile Richards, a Texas native, made the comment in an interview during The Texas Tribune Festival that aired Wednesday. Limits on abortion access earlier this year spurred legal battles.

rows.title: Texas court tosses death sentence in police killing due to intellectual disability
rows.standfirst: The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals resentenced Juan Lizcano to life in prison without the possibility of parole. He is at least the sixth death row inmate whose sentence was reduced after the U.S. Supreme Court slammed Texas’ methods for determining intellectual disability.

rows.title: Share of positive COVID-19 cases as Texas reopened was higher than originally reported, new state calculations show
rows.standfirst: Public health experts say discrepancies in key metrics, such as the positivity rate, made it difficult for officials to make informed policy decisions.

rows.title: TribCast: Texas again changes how it reports coronavirus data, and voting issues make their way through the courts
rows.standfirst: In this week’s TribCast, Matthew speaks with Ross, Emma and Shannon about another change in how Texas reports its coronavirus data and the legal fights related to voting that have reached the state Supreme Court.

rows.title: Watch former U.S. Defense Secretary Robert Gates discuss presidents, power and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: Gates also talked about how the pandemic is reshaping alliances.

rows.title: New voter registrations plummeted during the pandemic in Texas, where you can’t register online
rows.standfirst: Groups on both sides of the aisle say it’s harder to register voters when you can’t go door to door and big public events are canceled. Registration was down 24% in the first seven months of this year, compared with the same period in 2016.

rows.title: How years of underfunding public health left Texas ill prepared for the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Budget cuts meant skimpier caches of protective equipment, and Texas’ chronic shortage of public health workers has made the response more difficult, experts said.

rows.title: Faceless avatars and microphone malfunctions: A Houston teacher wonders if his students are learning
rows.standfirst: Spend a day with Westfield High School teacher Cris Hernandez, and you’ll see the frustrations and uncertainties of virtual teaching. More than four weeks into the school year, he still can’t tell if he’s connecting with his students.

rows.title: Democratic allies fighting to flip Texas House join forces for $1.1 million digital ad campaign
rows.standfirst: The campaign will benefit 11 candidates in some of the most pivotal races to take control of the lower chamber.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott loosens coronavirus restrictions for restaurants and other businesses in most regions of Texas
rows.standfirst: Restaurants, retail stores and office buildings will now be able to operate at 75% capacity, Abbott said. Three regions — the Rio Grande Valley, Laredo and Victoria — were excluded from the loosening of restrictions, however.

rows.title: Six months into the pandemic, out-of-work Texans are still struggling to navigate unemployment system
rows.standfirst: As 1.8 million Texans continue to claim unemployment, many complain they still can’t reach the Texas Workforce Commission and are quickly losing trust in Congress to agree to a second stimulus agreement.

rows.title: State releases numbers showing low Texas public school infection rates, but the data is limited
rows.standfirst: The state’s first effort to publicly report coronavirus data from schools shows low statewide infection rates. Breakdowns by school districts should be reported next week.

rows.title: Texas will allow visitations at nursing homes, other long-term care facilities with active COVID-19 cases
rows.standfirst: Visitors previously were allowed only into long-term care facilities where there were no active cases of the virus among residents and no confirmed cases among staff members in the past two weeks.

rows.title: Voting in Texas during the pandemic: Everything you need to know about the 2020 general election
rows.standfirst: Use The Texas Tribune’s voter guide to learn more about voting during the pandemic, mail-in voting, voting in person, Texas candidates and key dates for the 2020 general election.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas reopenings tied more to COVID-19 severity than to spread
rows.standfirst: Leaving behind their focus on the spread of the coronavirus, Texas leaders now say hospitalizations will guide their decisions on how to regulate social distancing at businesses and cultural centers.

rows.title: Texans with disabilities are eligible for mail-in voting, but people must decide for themselves if they qualify
rows.standfirst: Disability rights activists say they’re worried the confusion may deter at-risk Texans from voting or cause them to needlessly put their health at risk to show up in person at the polls despite being eligible for mail-in voting.

rows.title: August unemployment rate in Texas drops to 6.8%, lowest level since coronavirus shutdowns
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Labor Department on Friday announced Texas’ unemployment rate for August fell to 6.8%. That is still far above pre-pandemic levels, underscoring a summer of steady joblessness for many Texans.

rows.title: Republican U.S. House campaign arm cancels $2 million in Houston-area advertising
rows.standfirst: The region is home to multiple competitive races, including Congressional District 7 where Republicans are seeking to unseat U.S. Rep. Lizzie Fletcher

rows.title: Ted Cruz dismisses concerns over Attorney General Bill Barr and the federal coronavirus response as politically motivated
rows.standfirst: Cruz said that Barr has done an “admirable job” and that the Trump administration took “serious and … extraordinary” steps to fight the pandemic.

rows.title: Appeals court sides with Harris County in lawsuit over mailing absentee ballot applications
rows.standfirst: Harris County’s plan to send applications for mail-in ballots to all its voters was cleared by an intermediate appeals court, but it remains on hold until the Texas Supreme Court can rule.

rows.title: Texas courts must start telling tenants how a federal eviction moratorium can keep them housed
rows.standfirst: The Texas Supreme Court ordered that eviction citations will have to inform renters about the moratorium requirements and include the form needed to apply for protection.

rows.title: Conservative megadonor backs Shelley Luther for Texas Senate with $1 million loan
rows.standfirst: Luther, the Dallas salon owner who was jailed earlier this year over her refusal to close her business due to coronavirus restrictions, is running to replace state Sen. Pat Fallon, R-Prosper.

rows.title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg, U.S. Supreme Court justice, dies at 87
rows.standfirst: Nominated in 1993 by former President Bill Clinton, the liberal justice was the legal force behind many of the successes of the women’s movement. In her later years, she became something of a cult figure in legal and feminist circles.

rows.title: Ted Cruz and John Cornyn indicate support for confirming a new Supreme Court justice before the election
rows.standfirst: If the U.S. Senate confirms a nominee of President Donald Trump, it could secure a conservative influence on the high court for a generation.

rows.title: Texas bars and distilleries rip Gov. Greg Abbott for leaving them out of “unacceptable” reopening plan
rows.standfirst: While restaurants are allowed to expand to 75% capacity, those in the bar industry worry prolonged shutdowns could lead to 30% of its businesses closing within six months.

rows.title: Texas Tribune photojournalists on the front line: photography in a year of pandemic and unrest
rows.standfirst: Photojournalists are regularly in the thick of things when they cover stories, but 2020 has made their jobs even more difficult. Here’s a look at the work of five Tribune photographers in this extraordinary year — and some of the gear they’ve used.

rows.title: From abortion access to immigration, the battle over the open Supreme Court seat will affect Texas for a generation
rows.standfirst: Just days after the death of Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Republicans and Democrats are already engaged in an expensive and divisive fight over the future of the Supreme Court.

rows.title: Analysis: COVID-19’s almost incomprehensible toll in Texas
rows.standfirst: We’ve lost a lot of Texans already and will surely lose more to the coronavirus. Doesn’t it seem like there should at least be a moment of silence?

rows.title: Watch U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw talk about the 2020 election and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: Crenshaw, R-Houston, also talked about his first term in office and his own bid for reelection.

rows.title: Texas needs more poll workers this year because of the pandemic. Here’s how to become one.
rows.standfirst: Working at polls is going to look different this year. Find out what poll workers do, who qualifies to be one and how to become one yourself.

rows.title: UH Hobby School Launches Center with $6.5 Million Endowment
rows.standfirst: The UH Hobby School Establishes Elizabeth D. Rockwell Center on Ethics and Leadership with a $6.5 million endowment.

rows.title: High-speed train between Dallas and Houston gets federal approval
rows.standfirst: The railroad plans to connect Texas’ two biggest cities within 90 minutes. Construction could begin in the first half of next year.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Dan Crenshaw calls expanding mail-in voting “playing with fire” despite rarity of voter fraud
rows.standfirst: Crenshaw, a freshman Republican from Houston, made the comments in an interview during The Texas Tribune Festival that aired Monday. He also discussed immigration and changing voting patterns in Houston.

rows.title: As Texas college towns emerge as coronavirus hot spots, universities try to keep students from infecting locals
rows.standfirst: In counties where four-year college students make up at least 10% of the population, cases have grown 34% since Aug. 19, according to a Texas Tribune analysis. That’s compared with 23% in counties with a smaller proportion of students.

rows.title: Watch Stacey Abrams discuss voting rights, the census and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: The voting rights activist talked about increasing turnout, battling suppression, why a complete census count is so critical and her future plans.

rows.title: Trump says new TikTok headquarters could land in Texas, but questions about the deal remain
rows.standfirst: Shortly after Oracle — a California-based tech company with an Austin campus — emerged as a potential buyer last week, Gov. Greg Abbott tweeted that he had spoken to the president about Texas housing the possible new TikTok headquarters.

rows.title: Ted Cruz blocks a U.S. Senate resolution to honor Ruth Bader Ginsburg, citing a “partisan” amendment
rows.standfirst: The junior Texas senator objected to language his Democratic counterparts added noting that late U.S. Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg’s dying wish was that a successor not be chosen until after the presidential inauguration.

rows.title: Analysis: The 2020 election and Texas’ incremental blues
rows.standfirst: Democrats have their eyes on winning back the Texas House majority they lost in 2002. That wouldn’t give them the power to pass legislation, but it would give them the power to stop legislation they don’t like.

rows.title: For rural Texans, the Postal Service is a lifeline, but some say it’s been in decay for years
rows.standfirst: Business owners, farmers and local politicians said that they are more concerned with long-term problems than with the recent controversy surrounding the United States Postal Service.

rows.title: Watch Hillary Rodham Clinton on 2016, the 2020 election and more at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: The former U.S. secretary of state discussed the takeaways from her 2016 presidential campaign, what’s at stake in the general election and more about her career in public service.

rows.title: In a rare move, a Texas military veteran who was deported years ago was allowed back home. Now he’s a U.S. citizen.
rows.standfirst: Frank De La Cruz went to war with the U.S. Navy and came home with a drinking problem. Then he was arrested for driving while intoxicated, and the government kicked him out of the country.

rows.title: Republican Maryland Gov. Larry Hogan says it would be a mistake to push through a Supreme Court pick before the election
rows.standfirst: Speaking during a Texas Tribune Festival event, Hogan also said it would be a mistake for Democrats to pack the court.

rows.title: John Cornyn and MJ Hegar’s race is competitive in Texas, but they’re keeping a low profile compared to 2018’s Senate contest
rows.standfirst: Incumbent John Cornyn is pitching himself as a “steady hand on the wheel.” Democratic challenger MJ Hegar says that hand is driving Texas toward a cliff.

rows.title: Jay Hartzell officially named University of Texas at Austin president
rows.standfirst: The board approved an annual salary of $795,000 for Hartzell as interim president in June.

rows.title: Hillary Clinton says Democrats should frame fight for Supreme Court seat around health care
rows.standfirst: Speaking during The Texas Tribune Festival, Clinton said Democrats should play up the risks to health care access that could result from a more conservative high court overturning the Affordable Care Act.

rows.title: Texas Republicans sue to stop Gov. Greg Abbott’s extension of early voting period during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: State party Chair Allen West, Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller and members of the Texas Legislature were among those who filed the suit against Abbott.

rows.title: Conservative state Rep. Steve Toth withdraws support for Gov. Greg Abbott over coronavirus response
rows.standfirst: Toth, a member of the hardline Texas House Freedom Caucus, is the latest from that faction of the GOP to express disapproval of how Abbott has handled coronavirus-related shutdowns.

rows.title: When it rains, Texans forget drought and worsening water scarcity
rows.standfirst: After the pandemic, soaring population growth, development will again challenge planning and water supply.

rows.title: Texans curious about delays in election results, whether state is a battleground and attempts to increase Latino turnout
rows.standfirst: Five Texas Tribune political journalists answered questions on Reddit about the Nov. 3 general election.

rows.title: TribCast: How Ruth Bader Ginsburg’s death will affect Texas
rows.standfirst: On this week’s Tribcast, Matthew talks with Ross, Emma and Alex about the U.S. Supreme Court vacancy, Gov. Greg Abbott’s latest reopening announcement and voter registration in Texas.

rows.title: Texas begins letting people register to vote online when they’re updating their driver’s licenses
rows.standfirst: The limited move, ordered by a federal judge, marks the first time Texans have been able to register to vote online.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Ron Wright, who is sick with pneumonia, is released from hospital
rows.standfirst: The freshman Republican has been undergoing treatment for cancer since 2019.

rows.title: Dallas City Council increases police budget overall, but reallocates $7 million from overtime budget
rows.standfirst: Much of the overtime cuts were reallocated for other purposes in the department, including more than $3.8 million to hire nearly 100 civilian workers. Other new spending will go toward addressing root causes of crime and improving street lighting.

rows.title: As part of revived federal death penalty, Christopher Vialva executed for Texas double murder
rows.standfirst: Vialva was the seventh man executed in the federal execution chamber this year after a 17-year hiatus of the federal death penalty. Texas, meanwhile, is expected to have a comparatively low number of state executions this year because of the pandemic.

rows.title: More congressional action needed for strong recovery, former Trump economic adviser says
rows.standfirst: Gary Cohn said another round of federal coronavirus relief funding is needed to ensure a strong economic recovery.

rows.title: Health expert Peter Hotez warns of a third COVID-19 wave, says a vaccine likely won’t come for another year
rows.standfirst: The co-director of the Center for Vaccine Development at Texas Children’s Hospital talked during The Texas Tribune Festival about the hunt for a vaccine and how we can reopen safely.

rows.title: Watch state Rep. Sarah Davis and Democratic challenger Ann Johnson debate hurricane relief, flipping the House and more
rows.standfirst: In our “Split Decision” series, we asked the two attorneys about issues important to voters in this Houston-area district.

rows.title: Foreign hackers compromise Hamilton County’s email system, raising election security concerns
rows.standfirst: The malware attack, which sent fake email replies to voters and businesses who contacted officials in the Central Texas county, spotlights an overlooked vulnerability in counties that don’t follow best practices for computer security.

rows.title: Worried that flu season and coronavirus pandemic could overwhelm hospitals, health officials urge Texans to get flu shots
rows.standfirst: Health experts worry about testing shortages and crowded hospitals as flu season approaches in the midst of the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott wants to raise the stakes for protesters during a divisive Texas election
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s campaign event came after a majority of likely Texas voters in a recent poll said that law and order is a bigger issue than the pandemic. Yet they were also more likely to say that racism in the criminal justice system is a larger problem than riots in American cities.

rows.title: Texas Department of State Health Services withdraws data on school infections, citing “issues”
rows.standfirst: Data released this week showing reported coronavirus infection breakdowns by school district has been withdrawn by state health officials after “issues” were discovered.

rows.title: How a glitchy computer system skewed Texas’ coronavirus data and hampered its pandemic response
rows.standfirst: Local health officials describe the electronic system as “cumbersome,” “archaic” and “really slow,” though its performance has improved since it was upgraded in August.

rows.title: East Texas official arrested for alleged mail-in voter fraud involving 2018 Democratic primary for local seat
rows.standfirst: The indictments center on about 38 ballots or applications for ballots in a Gregg County Commissioners Court race. Experts say voter fraud is rare.

rows.title: Texas Republicans avoid criticizing Donald Trump for his electoral integrity comments
rows.standfirst: Many Republicans in Congress called for a peaceful transition of power if Trump loses, but did not engage directly with the president’s comments suggesting he might not accept the election results.

rows.title: Analysis: Coronavirus splits Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and his own party
rows.standfirst: Voting in the 2020 general election starts in Texas in less than three weeks. But the governor’s responses to the coronavirus have strained Republican unity.

rows.title: Republican dissent over Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s pandemic response animates state Senate special election
rows.standfirst: As Dallas salon owner Shelley Luther and state Rep. Drew Springer, R-Muenster, continue to spar ahead of Tuesday’s election, Luther directs some of her harshest criticism at Abbott.

rows.title: Coronavirus restrictions and remote learning may hamper college student voter turnout
rows.standfirst: Campaigns, political organizations and students at schools across Texas say they’re worried and frustrated that pandemic health restrictions are stymying efforts to register and turn out students to vote.

rows.title: Native American tribes in Texas rally to increase voter turnout
rows.standfirst: Native American tribe members say mistrust of the government and a history of erasure of indigenous people contribute to a lack of voter participation.

rows.title: Immigration policies hang in the balance as U.S. Senate prepares for fight over Ginsburg’s successor
rows.standfirst: President Trump hopes to quickly appoint a replacement for the liberal justice, and immigrant and civil rights groups are bracing for what could be years of losses in the high court.

rows.title: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from stopping census count next week
rows.standfirst: A federal judge in California late Thursday ordered that the census count should continue until Oct. 31, the date the Census Bureau had planned on before the administration abruptly shortened the count.

rows.title: How a local Texas politician helped a serial entrepreneur use COVID-19 to boost his business
rows.standfirst: In the early days of the coronavirus pandemic when testing supplies were limited, local politicians went to great lengths to help a businessman with a criminal past try to sell telehealth and COVID-19 services across Texas.

rows.title: A preeminent Christian research university
rows.standfirst: By Baylor University America’s earliest institutions of higher education — and others, like Baylor, founded in the 18th and 19th centuries — were created by Christian leaders who believed the combination of faith and academic excellence was essential in preparing men and women for professional achievement and the betterment of society. Over time, most of […]

rows.title: Race for Texas House majority has kept the contest for speaker quiet
rows.standfirst: No House members have declared their candidacy for speaker. Many say they have their sights set on November first as Democrats aim to flip the lower chamber.

rows.title: After Ginsburg’s death, high stakes for Texas’ legal challenge to the Affordable Care Act
rows.standfirst: Experts say the Supreme Court is unlikely to strike down the law in its entirety. Texas’ GOP leaders have yet to produce a promised plan to replace it.

rows.title: Texas will spend $171 million in federal coronavirus relief funds to help renters avoid evictions
rows.standfirst: The new program will provide rental assistance and legal aid for tenants who are behind on rent. Details on how Texans could apply or qualify weren’t immediately released.

rows.title: President Donald Trump nominates Amy Coney Barrett to U.S. Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: Both of Texas’ Republican U.S. senators have indicated they support moving forward with the Supreme Court confirmation process less than two months before the election.

rows.title: Federal judge blocks Texas’ elimination of straight-ticket voting
rows.standfirst: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said his office has filed a motion to stop the judge’s order and will file an appeal of the district court’s ruling.

rows.title: Texas woman says she was fired by Whataburger for wearing a Black Lives Matter mask
rows.standfirst: Similar cases are popping up elsewhere in the state. Over the summer, two Texas teachers faced disciplinary action from their schools, one for wearing a mask and the other for displaying a Black Lives Matter sign, among others, in her virtual classroom.

rows.title: Out of savings and without enough money for food, this North Texas woman is running out of options
rows.standfirst: Carrie Mansfield says that while more relief from the government would be welcome, she really just wants to get back to work. Listen in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: Analysis: Keep calm and vote on
rows.standfirst: Political people in high places are sowing doubt about voting and elections, making our 200-year-old system seem fraught with problems and even crime. Vote anyway.

rows.title: Making Texas’ medical cannabis laws more patient-friendly
rows.standfirst: By Morris Denton Texas Original Compassionate Cultivation Chief Executive Officer of Texas’ Original Compassionate Cultivation (TOCC). TOCC is the leading licensed medical cannabis producer in Texas, working alongside physicians to provide the highest quality cannabis medicine to patients and families seeking relief across the state. In 2015, Texas established the Compassionate Use Program (CUP), which […]

rows.title: Houston Republicans sue to limit in-person and absentee voting options in Harris County
rows.standfirst: Conservative activist Steve Hotze and a number of Republican candidates and officials are asking the Texas Supreme Court to shorten the early voting period and limit drop-off locations for absentee ballots in the state’s largest Democratic county.

rows.title: Williamson County sheriff charged with felony evidence tampering in Javier Ambler case
rows.standfirst: Last year, Williamson County sheriff’s deputies held Ambler down and stunned him four times with a Taser before his body went limp. It was filmed for a police reality TV show.

rows.title: Federal appeals court temporarily blocks ruling that reinstated straight-ticket voting in Texas
rows.standfirst: A federal judge’s ruling temporarily reinstating the practice of one-punch voting has been put on a temporary hold as judges on the U.S. 5th Circuit Court of Appeals weigh the issue.

rows.title: Watch H.R. McMaster on the pandemic and foreign policy challenges at The Texas Tribune Festival
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump’s former national security adviser also talked about his forthcoming book and America’s standing in the world.

rows.title: Veteran, war hero, defendant, troll: Man who raised millions for border wall uses social media to attack his detractors
rows.standfirst: Brian Kolfage, who’s charged in a case where he’s accused of defrauding thousands in a “build the wall” effort, has used personal attacks and misinformation against perceived opponents.

rows.title: As Texas reopens, border leaders say restrictions at international bridges should be lifted
rows.standfirst: Local leaders say the federal government’s decision to extend a ban on nonessential travel across the U.S.-Mexico border is crippling their budgets and local businesses.

rows.title: State GOP Chair Allen West calls on Donald Trump to visit Texas before Election Day
rows.standfirst: “I’ve got the message up to him,” said Allen West, who took over as party chair in July. “I’d like to see the president come back to Texas one more time, especially come back to North Texas.”

rows.title: Sam Houston State, Texas State University System to hire contact tracers as experts warn of a fall COVID-19 surge
rows.standfirst: The state is partnering with the Texas State University System to add roughly 200 new staffers to its stable of more than 3,500 contact tracers.

rows.title: Federal court orders Texas prison system to provide hand sanitizer for some geriatric inmates during pandemic
rows.standfirst: Texas has had more inmate deaths related to the coronavirus than any other prison system in the nation. Its death toll of at least 162 inmates outranks every other state as well as the federal prison system.

rows.title: Dr. Anthony Fauci says Americans should trust credibility of COVID-19 vaccine process
rows.standfirst: Fauci, the director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, blamed “mixed messages that have come out of Washington” for waning public trust.

rows.title: Republicans Shelley Luther, Drew Springer head to runoff in special election to replace state Sen. Pat Fallon
rows.standfirst: Much of the drama in the rapid-fire race had centered on Luther, a Dallas salon owner, and Springer, a state representative.

rows.title: Analysis: Unlike the 2018 election in Texas, 2020’s top races won’t set spending records
rows.standfirst: Two years ago in Texas, interest and election turnout were juiced by a $125 million race for U.S. Senate. This year’s ballot is topped by an extraordinary race for president, but the political spending at the top won’t match 2018.

rows.title: MJ Hegar raises $13.5 million in third quarter, a huge improvement over past hauls
rows.standfirst: The latest haul by the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate is almost eight times her previous best fundraising quarter.

rows.title: No straight-ticket voting for Texas’ 2020 election, federal appeals court says
rows.standfirst: A three-judge panel on the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a 2017 state law ending the popular one-punch option — and admonished a lower court judge for trying to bring the practice back so soon before early voting starts Oct. 13.

rows.title: Journalist Bob Woodward says pandemic, economy will decide 2020 election
rows.standfirst: At the keynote event of the 2020 Texas Tribune Festival, Woodward discussed the process of reporting out his latest book on the Trump presidency.
